Hi Emma — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. I put together a short explainer and a sample mapping table attached (billing_unit_mapping.xlsx) and included the current public rate card for hosted API (Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_2026_Q3.pdf). Key points up front:  

- Responses (new unified endpoint) is billed on "token-equivalent units" that align closely with chat-style requests, but we expose the mapping so teams can convert tokens to units for budgeting.
- Chat Completions and legacy endpoints historically used raw token counts with different per-token multipliers; our billing now converges but there are opt-in discounts and bundle pricing for legacy customers during migrations.
- Streaming does not change the underlying billed units — units are based on total billed tokens (prompt + response), but streaming can reduce perceived latency and improve throughput (affects cost via batching, not unit math).

I'll paste a short worked example below and attach the spreadsheet with more variants. If you want a one-page PDF mapping tailored to BrightLane's mix (short prompts + long responses), we can produce that for procurement.

Worked example (simplified):
- Prompt: 40 tokens
- Model generates: 960 tokens
- Total tokens billed: 1000 tokens
- Mapping rule (Responses endpoint): 1 billing unit = 100 tokens -> billed units = 10 units
- If hosted API rate = $0.012/unit (public list) -> charge = $0.12 for that request

Notes:
- Legacy chat endpoint used to bill per 1 token = 0.01 unit for some older customers; we converted these to the unit model above with migration credits.
- Committed monthly commit will yield stepped discounts on per-unit price (see attached rate card). For example, at a $30k/month commit, the per-unit price typically moves from $0.012 to $0.009 (subject to contract).

Hi Emma — quick answers to your two questions: 

1) Unit granularity: Yes, we can offer alternative unit sizing for committed customers. The public default is 100 tokens/unit because it simplifies billing and reporting, but for customers with many short-turn interactions we can do 25 tokens/unit or even 10 tokens/unit as part of a negotiated package. Pricing adjusts to reflect the greater granularity (slightly higher per-unit price but often lower total cost because of reduced rounding inefficiency).

2) Streaming behavior: Billing is based on the total tokens consumed by the model (prompt + all streamed response tokens). If your client opens and closes streams multiple times for what is logically a single generation, that will be counted as multiple requests and thus multiple billing events. That said, our SDK supports resumable streaming and continuous sessions which you can use to avoid artificial multiple-billing scenarios.

We can walk through sample runs from your logs and map them to expected monthly units to recommend the best unit size and discount tier. Vanessa — I put a placeholder for Monday 10:00 AM PST on my calendar. Emma — does that work?
